note: GH-009 retry publication safely: a retry plans against what the channel already holds. An asset present with the identical digest is skipped - the same bytes under the same name cannot produce a different channel state, and skipping is what makes the retry idempotent - while an asset present with different bytes is refused as a conflicting publication rather than overwritten, because that is not a retry but a different artifact wearing a published name. The test drives a real partial publication: an upload fails, the retry plan finds one identical asset and two missing ones, and the remainder completes to the state a single successful publication would have produced with each asset uploaded exactly once. A retry against a fully published channel needs nothing at all, which is what makes repeating it harmless. Fault proof: treating an asset with different bytes as already published makes the conflict undetectable and the refusal assertion fail (exit 1); the first attempt at this fault did not compile, which is a compile error and not a fault, and was retaken; revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
